title: The Silent Passenger of the Kalu Ganga: A Sri Lankan River Tale
description:
The Kalu Ganga, Sri Lanka's Black River, holds many mysteries in its murky depths. Tonight, we share an unsettling tale whispered among the old folk of Pelawatta village – the story of Kalu Banda, a simple boatman, and a passenger he picked up one fateful, misty night.

This is a fictional story, inspired by the eerie quiet of Sri Lankan rivers and the urban legends that grow along their banks. Join us as we navigate the chilling currents of fear and the unknown.
fiction_note: This is a fictional story inspired by Sri Lankan urban legends; characters and events are dramatised.

scenes.narration: Have you ever felt the river watching you? The Kalu Ganga, she carries so many stories, secrets whispered into her murky depths, especially after the sun dips low. Old Kalu Banda, he knew that river like the lines etched on his own palm, like his very breath. For forty long years, he’d ferried folks across her currents, seen every moon phase, every furious downpour, every calm, star-dusted night. But that particular night, it felt… different. Past midnight, the air was heavy, damp, the kind that clings to your skin. His old wooden boat, tied near the Pelawatta landing, bobbed gently against the river’s slow pulse. Frogs croaked their lonely, insistent songs from the muddy banks. Kalu Banda was tired, his muscles aching, ready for his last cup of plain tea and the deep, dreamless sleep he craved. He just wanted to go home, to the small kerosene lamp burning low on his verandah.
visuals: Wide shot, Kalu Ganga at deep night, thick mist obscuring distant banks, single small wooden boat with a dim kerosene lantern near a muddy landing, 35mm film, long exposure.
Detail shot, Kalu Banda's gnarled hands resting on the rough wooden edge of his boat, reflection of a flickering lantern in the dark river water, mist swirling at surface level.

scenes.narration: Then, from the deep shadows clinging to the ancient jak tree, a figure emerged. Not a rustle of leaves, not a crunch of gravel beneath their feet, just… there. As if the darkness itself had solidified. Dressed in clothes so dark they seemed to absorb the faint light, a wide-brimmed hat pulled low, entirely obscuring their face. Tall, slender, unnervingly silent. They simply stood at the water's edge, a stark silhouette against the faint, swirling mist rising from the river. Kalu Banda blinked, rubbing his tired eyes. Who would be out here at this hour? He cleared his throat. "Going across, aiya?" he called out, his voice cutting sharply through the quiet. The figure merely nodded, a slight, almost imperceptible movement. No greeting, no words. Just a silent, expectant presence. A prickle of unease, cold and sharp, started on Kalu Banda's skin.
visuals: Wide shot, a dark, cloaked silhouette standing absolutely still at the misty edge of the Kalu Ganga river bank at night, distant Kalu Banda and his boat, 50mm lens, subtle haze.
Detail shot, the hem of a dark, heavy cloak barely visible above muddy riverbank, mist swirling around unseen feet, faint light from a distant lantern just touching the fabric.

scenes.narration: The passenger stepped into the boat, not a sound disturbing the night. No creak of wood, no splash of water, just a gradual occupation of space. The boat, 'Kumari,' known for its gentle sway, didn't even shift much under their weight, which Kalu Banda found profoundly unsettling. It was as if they possessed no true mass. He pushed off, the familiar rhythm of the old oars dipping smoothly into the dark, silent water. "Where to, mahattaya?" he asked, trying to infuse his voice with cheerfulness he didn't feel. The figure pointed then, a slow, deliberate gesture, further downstream, beyond the familiar village lights, towards the thickest, darkest part of the jungle on the far bank. "Just… there," a low murmur, barely a whisper. Kalu Banda frowned. There was nothing there. No path, no huts, no village, no reason for anyone to go to that desolate, forgotten spot.
visuals: Wide shot, small wooden ferry boat moving across the dark Kalu Ganga, Kalu Banda rowing, the cloaked passenger a still silhouette in the bow, their arm faintly raised pointing towards a distant, dense jungle bank in thick mist, 85mm lens.
Detail shot, the dark, still silhouette of the passenger's back inside the boat, the dim light of Kalu Banda's lantern casting long shadows, their arm extended towards the dark river ahead.

scenes.narration: The mist grew thicker now, a living thing, swirling and coiling around the lantern’s faint, struggling glow, painting the river in shifting shades of grey. The air turned colder, not a natural chill, but a damp, heavy cold that felt wrong, unnatural, seeping into Kalu Banda's very bones. He pulled his sarong tighter, shivering despite the exertion. The usual night sounds—the distant drums from the temple, the endless chirping of crickets—they seemed muted, swallowed by the increasing, profound silence of this unsettling journey. Only the rhythmic creak of his oars, like a heartbeat, broke the oppressive spell. He glanced back at his passenger, a quick, furtive look. Still, silent, utterly motionless. He couldn’t shake the terrifying feeling that they weren’t quite… solid. Not quite 'there' in the way a living person should be.
visuals: Wide shot, the small boat now enveloped in dense river mist, only the faint glow of the lantern visible as a halo, Kalu Banda's silhouette rowing, the passenger's silhouette barely visible, soft focus, long exposure.

Detail shot, Kalu Banda's back as he rows, illuminated by the single kerosene lantern inside the boat, mist curling around his shoulders, his breath visible in the cold air, dampness on the wooden planks.

scenes.narration: Kalu Banda knew this stretch of the Kalu Ganga intimately, better than he knew his own hand. He knew every shifting sandbank, every treacherous submerged log, every small village landing. But the direction this passenger pointed, with that unsettling, silent gesture, it was far past all the known places. Deep into the jungle, where the mangroves grew impossibly thick, their roots like gnarled fingers gripping the water, and the land itself was swampy, desolate, utterly uninhabited by human folk. He tried again, his voice strained, a tremor he hoped the mist would swallow. "No good path there, mahattaya," he ventured, trying to reason. "No houses, no clear ground. Only wild things." The figure didn’t answer, of course. Just a faint, almost imperceptible inclination of the head, a subtle, unwavering urge forward. Kalu Banda’s heart began to beat a quick, uneven rhythm against his ribs, like a trapped bird.
visuals: Wide shot, the boat is now close to a completely desolate, jungled river bank, thick mangrove roots dipping into the dark water, no signs of human habitation, heavy mist, lantern light struggling to penetrate.
Detail shot, Kalu Banda's hand tightly gripping a rough wooden oar, his knuckles white, the reflection of the dark, unsettling river in the water directly beneath the boat.

scenes.narration: A strange, oppressive weight settled in the boat now, a palpable presence that seemed to press down on the wooden planks. It felt heavier, far heavier, as if carrying more than just two men. The old kerosene lantern, usually so steadfast, flickered wildly, the flame struggling against an unseen draft, casting long, dancing shadows that stretched and shrank like hungry hands. Kalu Banda felt goosebumps rise sharply on his arms, a cold wave washing over him. He could smell the damp, decomposing earth, the rich, almost sickly-sweet scent of night-blooming weeds from the jungle, cloying and heavy. The water, usually so familiar, now seemed blacker, deeper, reflecting no stars, no sliver of moon, only an abyssal darkness. He felt a profound sense of wrongness, a cold, unshakeable certainty that he was rowing into something ancient, something that didn't belong to the living.
visuals: Wide shot, the boat appearing unusually low in the water, heavy and sluggish, surrounded by thick, oppressive mist on the Kalu Ganga at deep night, jungle wall looming on the bank, soft, eerie glow from the lantern.
Detail shot, a flickering kerosene lamp inside the small wooden boat, its light casting dancing shadows on the wet planks, a faint, wispy tendril of mist curling around its base.

scenes.narration: "Are you sure, mahattaya?" Kalu Banda asked again, his voice lower this time, almost a desperate plea, barely above a whisper. "There is truly nothing for miles in that direction, only dense forest, no safe place to disembark." The passenger remained utterly still, a dark, unwavering silhouette against the deepening gloom. No reply. Not a breath, not a sigh, only that unsettling, absolute stillness. Kalu Banda's hands, gnarled and strong from years of rowing, tightened instinctively on the rough wood of the oars, his knuckles turning white. He swallowed, his throat suddenly dry, like sand. He remembered the old stories his grandmother used to tell, seated beside a flickering oil lamp, tales about the river at its darkest, about things that called to you from the shadows, things that weren't quite human.
visuals: Wide shot, Kalu Banda's back facing the camera, intensely focused on rowing, the dark, still silhouette of the passenger visible in the foreground, river mist curling between them, creating a sense of isolation.
Detail shot, the back of the passenger's head and shoulders, cloaked and dark, almost blending into the mist and darkness of the river night, with a faint, uneasy shimmer around the edges.

scenes.narration: Then, the passenger slowly raised a hand, a pale, almost translucent gesture, pointing directly towards a specific spot on the riverbank. It was nothing but a wall of tangled mangrove roots, thick with mud and slime, dense jungle rising behind it like a hungry, shadowed maw. There was no landing there, no sign of human passage, no clearing, just an impenetrable darkness. "Here," the whisper came again, colder this time, devoid of any human warmth, a dry, rasping sound. Kalu Banda froze. He could not, would not, take anyone to such a place. He looked down at the outstretched hand, and suddenly, in the faint, trembling light of his kerosene lantern, he truly saw it. Not quite a hand, not the solid, flesh-and-blood hand of a man, but something longer, bonier, the skin drawn taut and thin, almost skeletal. A ghost of a hand.
visuals: Wide shot, the boat very close to a desolate, muddy river bank, dense, dark jungle with tangled roots forming an impenetrable wall, a pale, almost glowing hand pointing from the boat towards the bank, ethereal light.
Detail shot, a pale, long-fingered hand, almost skeletal, dimly lit by a lantern, pointing towards a dark, muddy bank with thick, gnarled roots, the texture of the roots visible in the faint light.

scenes.narration: A scream, thick and choked, caught in Kalu Banda's throat, refusing to escape. His mind reeled, a whirlwind of ancient fears and terrible understanding. With a desperate jerk, he dropped one oar, hitting the black water with a sharp splash, the only sound breaking the ghastly silence. He fumbled wildly for the other. Fear, raw and instinctive, flooded every fibre of his being, cold and absolute. He didn’t question, didn’t think. He turned the boat with a frantic thrust of his remaining oar, pulling with all his might, rowing back towards the faint, distant glow of Pelawatta. He rowed like a madman, water churning violently, his breath coming in ragged, desperate gasps. He didn’t dare look back, but he felt their presence, a chilling, immense weight, still in the boat, still silent, still watching him.
visuals: Wide shot, the small wooden boat violently turning in the dark, misty Kalu Ganga, water churning from desperate oar strokes, Kalu Banda's frantic silhouette visible, the passenger's form still and dark in the boat, 35mm film, motion blur.

Detail shot, Kalu Banda's face, seen from behind, head turned slightly, eyes wide with terror, lit by the flickering lantern, beads of sweat on his forehead, his mouth slightly open in a silent scream.

scenes.narration: Kalu Banda didn't stop until the bow of his boat scraped with a sickening crunch against the familiar, muddy bank of the Pelawatta landing. He leaped out, stumbling onto the firm earth, his legs weak and trembling beneath him. He spun around, clutching the boat's rope like a lifeline, panting, eyes wide and wild, searching desperately. The boat bobbed gently on the dark water, silent, empty. The passenger was gone. No sound of footsteps, no ripple in the water, no trace, no hint they had ever been there. Just the lingering, cold, heavy air where they had been sitting. The lantern still flickered inside the small boat, casting long, dancing shadows that seemed to mock his utter terror. The Kalu Ganga flowed on, dark and indifferent.
visuals: Wide shot, the small wooden boat empty, nudged against the familiar, muddy Pelawatta landing, Kalu Banda's figure a hunched silhouette further up the bank, looking back at the boat, thick river mist, dawn light just beginning to break.
Detail shot, the inside of the now empty wooden boat, a single kerosene lantern still flickering on the floorboards, casting long, unsettling shadows on the wet wood, a sense of lingering presence.

scenes.narration: Kalu Banda never ferried another soul across that river after midnight. Not ever. The memory of that night, the whisper, the skeletal hand, it etched itself deep into his very being. He sold his boat a few months later, for a pittance, his face forever etched with a profound fear that never quite left him, not even in bright sunlight. Old people in Pelawatta still whisper about it, their voices low and serious, especially when the mist rolls in thick and heavy over the river. They say some things are best left undisturbed in the dark, ancient heart of the Kalu Ganga. They say some passengers aren't looking for a village, not for a home, but for something else entirely, something far older and hungrier. And if you, my friend, ever hear a faint, cold whisper from the river at night, asking to be taken to a place where there are no homes… for your own sake, don't answer.
visuals: Wide shot, the Kalu Ganga river at night, covered in dense, low-lying mist, no boats on the water, only the dark, silent river flowing under a sliver of moon, a deep sense of mystery and quiet dread.
Detail shot, a single, old, worn wooden oar, abandoned on a muddy river bank, partially obscured by mist, suggesting a story untold or a journey unfinished.

shorts.title: The Kalu Ganga's Silent Passenger
shorts.narration: Have you ever heard the old stories about the river, about what waits when the night gets truly dark? Kalu Banda, the old boatman, knew the Kalu Ganga like his own reflection. But one night, a silent passenger stepped into his boat. No words, just a gesture, pointing to a stretch of bank where no village stood, just a wall of tangled jungle. Kalu Banda felt the air grow cold, the boat grow heavy. Then, a pale, almost skeletal hand pointed to an empty, muddy patch. "Here," a whisper, cold as death. Kalu Banda looked at that hand, and an instinctive scream caught in his throat. He knew, with terrifying certainty, this passenger wasn't looking for a home. The full story is on our channel.

Vertical shot, Kalu Banda's back as he rows, illuminated by a single kerosene lantern inside the boat, mist curling around him.
Vertical shot, detail of a gnarled, strong hand on a wooden oar, water reflecting faint light beneath.
Vertical shot, dense, dark jungle bank seen through thick river mist, no clear path, just impenetrable foliage.
Vertical shot, silhouette of a cloaked figure in a small boat, facing away, mist swirling around them, light from a lantern barely visible.

shorts.title: The Boatman's Unseen Foe
shorts.narration: The Kalu Ganga, they say, keeps secrets. Old Kalu Banda, a boatman for decades, thought he knew them all. Until that night. A figure appeared from the shadows, silent, cloaked, asking to cross. But their destination, it was wrong. Past all the known villages, into the thickest part of the jungle, where only wild things lived. As Kalu Banda rowed, the river grew colder, the boat felt heavier. He tried to speak, but only silence answered. He looked back at his passenger, a dark shape against the mist. He felt a chill, a certainty that something ancient, something not quite human, was sharing his boat. The full story is on our channel.
visuals: Vertical shot, Kalu Ganga river surface, mist reflecting a very faint, distorted light from below, dark river banks on either side.
Vertical shot, a traditional Sri Lankan kerosene lamp on the wooden floor of a small boat, light spilling onto wet planks and dark water.
Vertical shot, a dark, draped silhouette standing at the edge of a river bank, mist swirling around their feet, waiting.
Vertical shot, Kalu Banda's tired, weathered face, lit from below by a lantern, eyes wide with dawning fear, looking towards the front of the boat (off-camera).
Vertical shot, dense, dark mangrove roots reaching into the black river water, partially obscured by mist, creating an ominous wall.
